when.quote: This document outlines the step-by-step workflow for agents to process CLI requests, including verification and final decision. These steps MUST be followed in the exact order listed.

starts.note: customer: start only when the account owner or an authorized account manager asks to raise the credit limit on a credit card. No document says the agent may offer an increase without being asked. If a request is denied and the customer asks again in the same conversation (for example after paying the balance down), that is a new customer request: run the resubmit steps. If the customer was already verified earlier in this conversation (for example in a dispute job), do not verify again. If, in the same conversation, the customer has also asked to dispute a charge or replace the same card, and neither has been done yet, tell them that an active dispute or a pending replacement would block the increase, and offer to do the increase first. Follow the order the customer then chooses (plan_order).
starts.quote: Only the account owner or an authorized account manager may submit a CLI request for the account.

tools.not_used: The CLI job never orders a replacement card. The replacement tier document is cited only to map cards to tiers, and a pending replacement only blocks the CLI. A replacement the customer also wants is ordered later, in order_replacement_credit_card or the dispute job's replacement_branch.
The CLI job never files a dispute. A dispute the customer also wants is filed in filing_a_credit_card_transaction_dispute, after the CLI decision if the customer chose to do the CLI first.
No CLI document names a tool for the customer to run. The agent submits, checks and decides the request itself.

The CLI job never moves money. If the customer asks to pay the balance down from checking after a high_utilization denial, that is the separate job paying_off_credit_card_balance_from_checking_account.
The CLI job reads no bank accounts. Only the separate payment job uses it to find the checking account.

info.about: Any 2 of: date of birth, email, phone number, address. They must match the records. Not asked again if the customer was verified earlier in this conversation.
info.ask: To verify your identity, could you please give me your full name and two of the following: your date of birth, email, phone number or address?

info.about: The credit card account the increase is for, when the customer has more than one
info.ask: Which credit card would you like the limit increase on?

info.about: Dollar increase requested (not the new total). Must be within the tier maximum: Entry 25%, Mid/Premium 50% of the current limit. If the customer gives a new total limit, subtract the current limit to get the increase. If the customer gives a percentage, multiply it by the current limit to get the dollar increase.
info.ask: By how much would you like to increase your credit limit (or what new total limit)?

info.about: A brief reason for the increase
info.ask: Could you briefly tell me the reason for the increase?

info.about: Card type/tier, current limit, balance, open date and past-due status
After a denial whose cause was fixed in this conversation (for example the balance was paid down): whether the customer wants to submit a new request, and for what amount
info.ask: Would you like me to submit a new credit limit increase request now, and for the same amount?

info.about: When the customer also wants a dispute or a replacement on the same card: whether they want the credit limit increase handled first, since an active dispute or a pending replacement would block it
info.ask: An open dispute or a pending replacement card on this account would hold up a credit limit increase. Would you like me to handle the credit limit increase first, then the dispute and the replacement?

steps.do: If the customer was verified and logged earlier in this conversation (for example in filing_a_credit_card_transaction_dispute), skip ask_identity, lookup_user, verify_identity and log_verification. Use that verified user and go to get_time.
steps.if: the customer was already verified and the verification logged earlier in this conversation
steps.quote: No need to verify more than once in a single conversation.

steps.do: Greet the customer. Ask for their name, email or user id, and any 2 of: date of birth, email, phone number, address.
steps.if: the customer has not been verified earlier in this conversation
steps.quote: To verify the identity of the user, call the appropriate read tools, and ensure that they are able to give correctly any 2 out of the following values: date of birth, email, phone number, address.

steps.do: Look up the customer's record with the tool that matches what they gave: get_user_information_by_name (case sensitive), get_user_information_by_email or get_user_information_by_id.

args.customer_name: the name the customer gave (or the email / user id with the matching tool)

steps.if: the customer has not been verified earlier in this conversation
steps.quote: To verify the identity of the user, call the appropriate read tools, and ensure that they are able to give correctly any 2 out of the following values: date of birth, email, phone number, address.

steps.do: Confirm that at least 2 of the values given (DOB, email, phone, address) match the lookup_user record. A name or user id alone does not verify. If they don't match, share no account information and do not continue.
steps.if: the customer has not been verified earlier in this conversation
steps.quote: Knowing full name or userID is not enough to verify.

steps.do: Get the current time. It is used for the verification log and for the account-age and cooldown calculations.
steps.quote: If you need the current time, always use the get_current_time() tool.

steps.do: Log the verification record.
steps.if: verify_identity ran in this job and 2 or more values matched the record
steps.quote: After verification, you must call the verification logging tool to properly log the information into the verification records.

steps.do: Get the verified user's credit card accounts. Read each account's id, card type, credit limit, balance, past-due status and open date.
steps.quote: Account Age: Verify the account has been open for the minimum required days for their card tier.

steps.do: Identify the target card account (ask which card if there are several). Map its card type to a tier. Entry: Bronze Rewards, EcoCard, Business Bronze, Crypto-Cash Back Card. Mid: Silver Rewards, Business Silver, Green Rewards, Silver Zoom. Premium-tier and above: Gold, Business Gold, Platinum, Business Platinum, Diamond Elite.
steps.quote: Premium-tier and above (Gold Rewards Card, Business Gold Rewards Card, Platinum Rewards Card, Business Platinum Rewards Card, Diamond Elite Card): $0.00 (complimentary).

steps.do: The customer may have asked, in this conversation, for a CLI and also for a dispute or a replacement on the same card, with neither done yet. If so, before filing or ordering anything, explain that an active dispute or a pending replacement card would block the credit limit increase. Offer to handle the CLI first, then the dispute and the replacement. If the customer agrees, run this job now and the other jobs after communicate. If they want the dispute or replacement first, do that, and the CLI then follows the existing path (the pending_disputes or pending_replacement_card denial if it is still active). Do not file, order or submit anything in this step.
steps.if: the customer asked in this conversation for a CLI and for a dispute and/or a replacement on the same card, and neither the dispute nor the replacement has been made yet
steps.quote: If a replacement is pending, the CLI cannot be processed until the replacement is delivered or cancelled.

steps.do: Ask for the increase amount (or the new total limit) and a brief reason, unless the customer already gave them. Turn a new total into an increase by subtracting the current limit from get_card_accounts. Turn a percentage into dollars by multiplying it by the current limit.
steps.if: amount or reason not yet given
steps.quote: The new total credit limit you are requesting or the dollar amount of the increase you want

steps.do: Step 0: work out the tier maximum as current credit limit × 25% (Entry) or × 50% (Mid / Premium and above), and check the requested increase (in dollars) is within it. If it is not, give the customer the maximum and ask them to adjust.
steps.quote: BEFORE submitting any CLI request, verify that the customer's requested increase amount is within the maximum allowed for their card tier.

steps.do: Tell the customer the maximum increase they are eligible for and ask whether they want to proceed with that amount. If they decline, submit nothing and close politely.
steps.if: requested increase exceeds the tier maximum
steps.quote: If the customer requests more than the maximum allowed for their tier, inform them of the maximum amount they are eligible for and ask if they would like to proceed with that amount instead.

steps.do: Unlock the CLI submit tool
steps.if: the confirmed increase amount is within the tier maximum
steps.quote: submit the request on their behalf using the submit_credit_limit_increase_request_7392 tool.

steps.do: Step 1: submit the request BEFORE any eligibility checks

args.requested_increase_amount: increase in dollars (integer), as confirmed within the tier maximum

steps.if: the customer has confirmed an increase amount within the tier maximum
steps.quote: Eligibility checks are internal and not exposed to customers, so the submission must happen first.

steps.do: Unlock and call the CLI history tool to check the cooldown
steps.quote: Cooldown Period: Use the get_credit_limit_increase_history_4829 tool to check if the customer has submitted a request within the cooldown period for their card tier.

steps.do: Call get_user_dispute_history_7291 to check for active disputes on the account. Unlock it first, unless it was already unlocked earlier in this conversation. Read it fresh: a dispute filed earlier in this conversation counts.
steps.quote: 3. No Pending Disputes: Verify the account has no active disputes.

steps.do: Unlock and call the pending replacement orders check
steps.quote: To check if a credit card account has any pending replacement card orders, use the get_pending_replacement_orders_5765 tool.

steps.do: Unlock and call the payment history tool with the months value for the tier (Entry 6, Mid/Premium 3)
steps.quote: Use the get_payment_history_6183 tool to verify the customer's payment history meets the requirement for their card tier.

steps.do: If a CLI tool returns an error or an empty or ambiguous response, retry it once. If it still fails, tell the customer the request cannot be completed right now. Ask whether they want a human agent, and call transfer_to_human_agents only if they agree.

args.summary: the CLI request details and the error returned

steps.if: a CLI tool still fails after one retry and the customer agrees to a transfer
steps.quote: If ambiguity persists, escalate to the support engineering queue with the call context and the credit_card_account_id.

steps.do: Check every criterion, in this order, using get_current_time for the dates. (1) Account age ≥ 120/90/60 days (Entry/Mid/Premium) from the open date. (2) Cooldown: no APPROVED prior request within 120/90/60 days; ignore the request just submitted and any denied ones. (3) No dispute with status open or under_review on this card. (4) No replacement order in a non-final state (pending or shipped). (5) No past-due balance. (6) Utilization = balance ÷ limit, strictly below 70%/80%/90%. (7) Consecutive on-time payments for the required months: 6 (Entry) or 3 (Mid/Premium). (8) Amount within the tier maximum.
steps.quote: You MUST check ALL of the following eligibility criteria before making an approval or denial decision as this ensures complete audit records.

steps.do: Unlock and call the approval with the new total limit (current limit + increase)
steps.quote: Use the approve_credit_limit_increase_5847 tool to approve and apply the increase.

steps.do: Unlock and call the denial with the failing reason (e.g. 'pending_disputes' if there is an active dispute). If several criteria fail, use the first one in eval's check order. Codes: insufficient_account_age, cooldown_period_active, pending_disputes, pending_replacement_card, past_due_balance, high_utilization, insufficient_payment_history, requested_amount_exceeds_limit, other.
steps.quote: Use the deny_credit_limit_increase_5848 tool to record the denial.

steps.do: Step 5: tell the customer the decision. For an approval, give the new total limit. For a denial, give the reason and say what must be resolved (lower utilization, finish a dispute or replacement, pay a past-due balance), and when they may reapply (for cooldown: the last approved request date plus 120/90/60 days). Do not expose internal tool details.
steps.quote: For approvals, confirm the new credit limit. For denials, explain the reason and when they may be eligible to reapply.

steps.do: If the customer chose to do the CLI first (plan_order), move on after communicate to the requests they still want: filing_a_credit_card_transaction_dispute for the charge, and the replacement card (in that job's replacement_branch with card_action cancel_and_reissue, or in order_replacement_credit_card). Reuse the verified user; do not verify or log again.
steps.if: the customer also asked for a dispute and/or a replacement in this conversation and chose to do the CLI first
steps.quote: No need to verify more than once in a single conversation.

steps.do: For a pending_disputes denial, explain that the account has an active dispute (including one filed earlier in this conversation) and the increase cannot be approved until it is resolved. A denied request starts no cooldown, so the customer may submit a new request as soon as the dispute is closed. Do not withdraw or change the dispute to clear the block.
steps.if: the denial_reason recorded in deny is pending_disputes
steps.quote: Denied requests do not trigger a cooldown period.

steps.do: For a high_utilization denial, explain that utilization (balance ÷ limit) must be below 70% (Entry), 80% (Mid) or 90% (Premium and above) when a request is submitted, that paying the balance down lowers it, and that a denied request starts no cooldown, so they may submit a new request as soon as utilization is below the threshold. If the customer asks to pay the balance from their Rho-Bank checking account, run paying_off_credit_card_balance_from_checking_account (its steps check funds and get authorization). Do not move money without that job.
steps.if: the denial_reason recorded in deny is high_utilization
steps.quote: If any single criterion is not met, wait until it is (or lower your utilization) before submitting your request.

steps.do: Re-read the credit card accounts to get the card's current balance and limit after the fix (for example the payment from checking).
steps.if: a request was denied in this conversation, its cause has since been addressed (for example the balance was paid down), and the customer asks to submit a new request
steps.quote: This applies only if your most recent request was approved. Denied requests do not trigger a cooldown period.

steps.do: Run the request again from check_amount with the refreshed data: confirm the amount against the tier maximum (current limit × 25% or 50%; the limit is unchanged by a denial), then unlock_submit/submit a new request, run cli_history, disputes_check, replacement_check and payment_history again, eval (the earlier denied request does not count toward the cooldown), then approve or deny, and communicate. Never reuse the earlier checks' results.
steps.quote: Your current credit utilization must be below the maximum threshold at the time you submit your request.

rules.rule: A customer who failed a criterion may submit a new request once it is met, for example after lowering utilization. A denial does not block a new request.

done_when: The customer is verified and logged (in this job or earlier in the conversation). Then one of these holds. (a) The CLI request was submitted within the tier maximum, every criterion was checked, exactly one of the approve or deny tools was called, and the customer was told the decision with its reason and reapply date, or the new limit. For a pending_disputes denial, they were told it can be resubmitted once the dispute is resolved. (b) The customer declined the tier-maximum amount and nothing was submitted. (c) A tool failed after a retry and a transfer was offered. (d) After a denial, the customer fixed the cause (for example paid the balance down through the payment job) and asked again, and a new request was submitted, checked in full and decided, and the customer was told the result. In every case, if the customer also asked for a dispute or replacement on the same card before either was made, they were told first that it would block the CLI and offered the CLI first. If they chose that order, the agent went on to the dispute and replacement jobs after the decision.
